threads.name: Pricing
threads.summary: Leaning towards seats: small teams want to know the bill up front. Still open is what the smallest plan costs.

frags.text: Usage-based feels fair on paper, but nobody can predict their bill.
Two small teams said they would rather pay per seat and know the cost up front.
If seats win, the real question is what the smallest plan should cost.

threads.next: Draft a one-page pricing outline for seats-only and send it to the two teams.

intentions.rawInput: I want to stop sitting on work until it's perfect.
intentions.expandedIntention: I am someone who ships small things often, and lets them be seen before they are finished.
recommendedActions: I show the work on the day it works, not the day it is perfect.
I cut the scope instead of moving the date.
I let the first version be small enough to actually leave my hands.
counterIntentions: I rewrite the same feature instead of releasing it.
I wait for a finished feeling that never arrives.
I call it research when I am avoiding the ship.

intentions.rawInput: I keep carrying the whole day home with me.
intentions.expandedIntention: I am someone who ends the day clear, because everything that mattered was written down once and trusted.
recommendedActions: I say the thought out loud the moment it arrives, and let it be filed.
I let a thing fade when it has stopped mattering.
I close the day by naming only what is actually next.
counterIntentions: I keep lists I never read again.
I re-decide the same thing three times a week.
I carry unfinished decisions into the night.
